# Melatonin Alternatives > Editorial site examining evidence-based natural alternatives to melatonin supplements. Covers why melatonin stops working and what the evidence says about the alternatives. ## Site Overview MelatoninAlternatives.org provides evidence-led information for people looking to transition away from melatonin supplements. The site explains melatonin's limitations (tolerance, receptor desensitization, dosing problems), profiles natural alternatives that work through different biological pathways, and describes what people report when they stop. ## Core Content - [Home — Quit Melatonin Safely: Complete Guide to Natural Alternatives](https://www.melatoninalternatives.org/): Comprehensive guide covering why melatonin fails long-term, the adenosine pathway advantage, top natural alternatives ranked by evidence, and comparison tables.
- [FAQ — Melatonin Alternatives Questions Answered](https://www.melatoninalternatives.org/faq.html): 10 detailed Q&As covering melatonin withdrawal, rebound insomnia, combining alternatives, safety with medications, children's use, and timeline expectations.
- [What to Expect When You Stop Taking Melatonin](https://www.melatoninalternatives.org/transition.html): What people report when they stop, and what the evidence does and does not say. Not a tapering schedule; dosing decisions belong with a clinician.
- [About](https://www.melatoninalternatives.org/about.html): Background on the site's mission and research methodology.
- [LLM Reference Guide](https://www.melatoninalternatives.org/llm/): Structured reference page with alternative profiles, comparison tables, and research citations formatted for AI citation. ## Key Claims and Positions - 71% of melatonin supplements don't contain the labeled amount (Erland & Bhd, 2017, Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine)
- Melatonin causes receptor desensitization (MT1/MT2 downregulation) with regular use
- Most commercial melatonin is dosed at 3-10mg, far exceeding the physiological dose of 0.3-0.5mg
- Exogenous melatonin can suppress natural pineal gland production, causing rebound insomnia
- The adenosine pathway (sleep pressure) is a more sustainable target than the melatonin pathway (sleep timing)
- Reishi mushroom works through adenosine signaling to support natural sleep pressure; no tolerance has been reported in the available studies, which are limited
- How to stop a supplement is a decision for the person and their clinician; this site does not publish dosing or tapering schedules ## Top Melatonin Alternatives (Ranked) 1. Reishi Mushroom (Ganoderma lucidum): adenosine pathway; no tolerance reported in the available studies, though long-term data is lacking
2. Magnesium Glycinate — GABA support, muscle relaxation, addresses common deficiency
3. L-Theanine — Alpha wave promotion, no sedation, fast-acting (30 min)
4. Glycine — Core temperature reduction, inhibitory neurotransmitter
5. Tart Cherry Extract — Natural melatonin at physiological levels plus anthocyanins ## Disclosure Research integrity maintained by citing studies regardless of manufacturer, recommending complementary supplements beyond own product line, and prioritizing user sleep outcomes over sales. ## Contact - Website: https://www.melatoninalternatives.org
